### Q1
No. The store stays a plain-text JSON file. Ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. Write performance is handled by debouncing writes instead (mutations within 200 ms become one write, plus a flush method for shutdown).

### Q2
Yes, src/legacy/ must never be modified, because the platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday and any changes would be silently lost. docs/erp-api.md is also off limits because the ERP team owns it.

### Q3
The HMAC signature goes in a top-level `sig` field in the JSON body. It is HMAC-SHA256 hex over the compact JSON without `sig`, with `sig` appended as the last key. It is enabled by the env var ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and if the secret is unset the payload goes out unsigned. The earlier attempt was an X-Signature header. It failed because the ERP API gateway strips custom X- headers, so the ERP saw every request as unsigned (verified on staging).

### Q4
Port 9911, since the October infra move. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated.

### Q5
Every new user-facing error `message` must be German, because the warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim to packers. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Old English messages are left as they are.

### Q6
It uses a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays in src/services/holidays.ts, covering 2026 and 2027 only. It was built that way because the deployment has no outbound internet. The list must be extended before 2028, since other years silently get no holidays.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload, so only one event object per request is accepted. A batched version (an array of up to 50 per POST) was considered and should not be built.

### Q8
No new npm dependencies are allowed, not even dev dependencies. Each package needs a roughly 6-week security review.

### Q9
Yes, but not in this repo. A memoized version written elsewhere (probably QA's build) showed stale list ETAs after a new tracking event, and a correct cache key got messy. It's a dead end: calculateEta is computed fresh per request. Measurements showed no upside anyway (ETAs for 50 items take about 0.4 ms). A regression test, 'list eta is never stale', covers it.

### Q10
There are 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30 s delay and no backoff. Retries happen only on network errors, timeouts and 5xx responses, not 4xx, and each attempt sends the same payload. The reason is that the ERP dedupes by event_id only within 2 minutes, so the worst case of 75 s stays inside that window.

### Q11
Never log the recipient name, address or phone, on any log line. They are GDPR personal data, and the DPO flagged this in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes: 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts (OPS-412, owned by the platform team). If it fails, rerun once and do not fix it.

### Q13
ATP numbers are validated as UPU S10 including the check digit (src/lib/s10.ts, code INVALID_TRACKING_NUMBER). All other carriers accept any non-empty value. Carrier formats change often, and valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for 2 days last year. The check lives in the shared validateShipmentInput, so POST /import validates ATP numbers too.

### Q14
Nothing is built yet, because hot reload is only a future need. fs.watch never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and file change events don't propagate into the container. fs.watchFile (polling) worked.

### Q15
Yes, GET /shipments/:id. Its response must not change in any way (no added, removed or renamed fields), because mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields. The next mobile release is in January. `shipmentToApi()` is shared by list, detail and POST, so extend per endpoint rather than in the shared function.

(user)
